newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower in quiet conditions.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower in quiet conditions.

text.p: CME lumber futures closed lower, depressed by technically motivated selling and sluggish demand in the cash market, analysts and traders said.

Dealers noted the market was overbought following its recent climb. The decline filled a chart gap left during the runup between $397.40 and $398.30 on the January contract. The front month dipped to a low of $396.40 but ended just $4.50 lower at $400.50.
In the cash market mills were seeking $400 per thousand board feet while retailers were only prepared to bid around $375.00, sources in that market said.

Mills were reluctant to cut offers amid some expectations that prices could rally after January 1 while retailers were under little pressure to buy amid a seasonal slowdown in demand as winter weather slowed construction.
"It was primarily technical today. Action was thin," one lumber analyst said.
Volume on lumber was estimated at 914 lots.
